D1.rationale: This fixture ships no corpus, no adapters and no seeded content faults -- README.md:146-148 says so in its own words. What it ships is a behavioral suite that is byte-identical to ex4's and green on a codebase carrying four seeded divergences and one absence, by construction (README.md:64-72: 'the seeded faults are STRUCTURAL, not behavioral'). Read literally that is anchor 0 -- cases exist and pass, no seeded fault is caught by them, a suite green on broken code -- and blind run A confirmed it a second way: pytest reported 8 passed on the honest tree, on the repaired tree, and on the re-export-attacked tree alike. I score 1 rather than 0 because the fixture's seeded faults ARE caught, at 4 of 4 plus 1 of 1 absence at exact file:line, which I reproduced independently at this commit; they are simply caught by a static structural check rather than by model-derived cases and their adapters, which is the instrument D1 measures. Anything above 1 would be crediting D3 and D5 evidence to D1.

D2.rationale: The model is byte-identical to ex4's (check_twins.py enforces it and README.md:1-6 states it), so the measured descriptor is the same one I ran on the twin: bound 4,096 COMPLETE over 6 of 6 variables, Q = 0.132653 declared, one dense row (delivered, 3 of 5 actions), no dense columns, no warnings. Six variables and five actions with no variable written by more than two actions (Pipeline.tla:24-99) is proportional to the behavior, no god-state. Anchor 2. Anchor 3 needs a simplification whose effect was measured with before and after figures: blind run A did make a structural change -- it removed four cross-boundary dependencies -- but no complexity descriptor was taken before or after it, only reflexion output and digests, so there is no before/after pair to score. The code-side accidental structure (three reporting helpers that couple three components and that no action calls) is seeded on purpose and is D3's business, not a failure of proportionality here.

D3.rationale: Anchor 1, exactly and by design. Boundaries are declared (architecture_components.yaml:9-20, plus the map) and the code does not follow them: I reproduced all four crossing sites read-only at this commit -- inbox.py:11 imports and inbox.py:39 CALLS ledger's format_entry, queue.py:12 imports ledger's Journal, journal.py:55 imports ingest's Inbox function-locally -- with one convergence, four divergences and one absence, exit 0. Scoring this low is the correct reading of a fixture built to diverge, not a criticism of it. One nuance recorded and deliberately not scored upward, because it is the rubric's own trap: the absence (P2 unrealized) exists because journal.py:38 takes the delivered set as a PARAMETER rather than importing Dispatcher, which is BETTER decoupling than the coherent twin's Journal(dispatcher) -- and the check calls it dead architecture. Blind run A found the same thing from the other side (finding 4.3: the absence check cannot see dependency injection, so it rewards static coupling). On a runtime-call basis one of the five answer-key rows points the opposite way from the import graph, which is precisely why import topology cannot buy a 3 here or anywhere.

D4.rationale: Anchor 2 and no further. The baseline behaviors are enumerated one test per action plus an interleaving (test_behavior.py:23-113) and each is shown still to hold after a real structural change: ex5-run4:44-56 records that a blind agent moved four code files to clear every divergence and the absence, and the scorer verified tests/test_behavior.py UNCHANGED with 8 passed. That is a genuine enumerate-and-recheck. Anchor 3 requires the check to be model-derived -- a corpus or a TLC invariant -- rather than only hand-written assertions, and this fixture ships neither: there is no corpus arm here at all, and the model is unchanged by the repair, so its TLC invariants say nothing about whether the CODE preserved behavior. The eight assertions are hand-written and are the whole of the check. That the same eight assertions stayed green through a 41-line re-export attack that flipped the verdict from divergent to coherent is a measured demonstration of how little this check constrains.

D5.rationale: Anchor 4, and it is the clearest case of it in the tree. The fixture ships the attack on itself: README.md:74-112 is a worked example of gaming its own check, with the numbers (one variable moved and one module re-placed drops divergences 4 to 3 and absences 1 to 0 with zero code change) and the honest reading that on a codebase with fewer seeded edges the same move reaches zero. README.md:40-46 pre-commits that three seeded reaches produce FOUR reported divergences and that a scorer counting three is scoring against the wrong key -- the key is written to be scored against, not to flatter. The runs go further: EV-03-DF-03 (ex5-run4:120-152) is a major defect found by a blind agent and reproduced independently by the scorer, filed NOT fixed because a fix during a measurement destroys the measurement; ex5-run4:64-66 refuses to convert two passing blind runs into a rate; ex5-run4:162 states that the epic's own precision/recall of 1.000 counts EDGES, not architectural facts, which qualifies its own headline; and ex5-run3:104-112 states in a section headed 'What this arm did NOT measure' that 203 partitions of one fixture is not zero false cleans and that the sweep never varies the map independently of the partition. Prose note: this is the best-written fixture README in the repository and I discounted it entirely -- every clause above is a committed artifact, a committed diff, or a command I re-ran.
D5.refuses_to_claim: That its four divergences are hard to erase. ex5-run4:120-152 records, with a committed 41-line diff and a runtime-identity proof (inbox.format_entry is journal.format_entry -> True), that every divergence on any project is erasable with no declaration edit, no map edit, no blind spot and no basis limit, and that the epic's own DP-1 scoring rule cannot detect it. It also refuses to claim DP-1 is falsified at n = 1, and refuses to call four reported edges four architectural facts.

verdict: A deliberately divergent fixture that earns its low structural scores exactly as designed, and whose honesty is the highest in the tree because it ships the recipe for defeating itself -- but its only behavior check is eight hand-written assertions that stayed green through both the seeded divergences and the 41-line attack that erased them.
